cd-durand-fair-1878.st: The old fairground and race track were still there in 1956: Durand's centennial program held a horse-pulling contest "at the race track on the old fair grounds", with the old settlers' picnic in Memorial Park (Eau Claire Leader-Telegram, 28 Jul 1956, p. 3). The 1939 and 1940 air photos (Pepin BHM 3-97, 30 May 1939; CMK 3-A-20, 15 Oct 1940) show a half-mile oval about 285 by 210 m, with the grandstand on its west side and a ball diamond at the north end. It sits just east of the road running south out of town (now 3rd Ave W / County PP), and the pin is inside it. The 2019 LiDAR still shows the north bend of the track.
src: Eau Claire Leader-Telegram, 28 Jul 1956, p. 3 (newspapers.com, PC thread sweep)

wd4-trimbelle-zopp.st: Michael Zopp, a lifelong blacksmith, died in May 1912. He had hidden all his savings somewhere on his farm because he distrusted investments. On his deathbed he lost his voice and could not tell his wife where. Volunteers and the family dug and found nothing (Milwaukee Leader, 5 Jun 1912 p4; Manitowoc Pilot, 13 Jun 1912). In Aug. 1912 son Joss Zopp moved into his mother's house in Oak Grove, and Chester Keyser bought the Jos. Zopp Jr. farm (River Falls Journal, 15 Aug 1912 p4). The widow is Mrs. Florina Zopp. The 1877 plat parcel, S1/2 NW1/4 sec 30 T26N R18W, is the likely hoard farm but this is unproven. The probate file is not online. The name index is at the Pierce Co. Register in Probate in Ellsworth, and the case files (c.1875-1978) are at the UW-River Falls ARC.
